input: Decode octopus temperature-dependent RNA editing (Birk et al., Cell 186:2544-2555, 2023, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2023.05.004) as a whole domain: 12 nodes, 132 ordered pairs, 20 non-neutral edges. Full decode: claude/DOMAIN_DECODE_OCTOPUS_RNA_EDITING.md.

rule_source: Rangan KJ et al. Cell 2023 (squid companion)
Liscovitch-Brauer N et al. Cell 2017 (plasticity vs genome evolution trade-off)
metadata.citation_correction: The X post lists authors as Birk, Rangan & Rosenthal; Rangan led the companion squid paper, not the octopus paper.

claims.text: Octopus bimaculoides increases A-to-I RNA editing at >20,000 sites in the cold, recoding >13,000 codons, many in neural proteins; shifts begin within hours.

A fast, reversible, environment-driven layer between fixed code and output retunes function without touching the code: RNA editing over DNA, adapters/prompts over base weights, acclimatization over genome, regulation over constitution.

Cost: heavy runtime recoding freezes the base where the recoding layer attaches. Cephalopod edit sites require conserved flanking sequence and slow genome evolution (Liscovitch-Brauer 2017); adapters only work on the base model they were trained for.
The most environment-exposed components receive the most runtime tuning (membrane-associated and Ca2+-binding proteins). AI analog untested.
Structural instance of SC-CP-001 (clay fixed, pot reshaped) and of the Octopus Protocol's namesake animal (SC-CT-001): distributed nervous system retuned locally at the molecular level.

flows: environment -> temperature -> ADAR -> edited mRNA -> recoded protein -> neural function

causal_validity.reason: Temperature -> editing -> protein function shown experimentally (synaptotagmin Ca2+ binding; kinesin transport velocity).

scale_integrity.reason: Strong at biology and AI; physical scale has no editor (residual).

boundary_integrity.reason: DNA/RNA boundary is where insulation holds; P1 confirmed.

measurement_integrity.reason: Peer-reviewed measurements; lab plus seasonal field corroboration.

wave_function_coherence.reason: Editing level and neural performance measured together; link to framework concept argued.

substrate_sovereignty.reason: Edits never write back to DNA.

corpus_completeness.reason: Octopus paper covered; squid companion paper referenced only.

prediction_tests.prediction: Heavy runtime recoding freezes the base where it attaches
Runtime recoding is orders of magnitude faster than base change
Most environment-exposed components get most tuning
Runtime recoding has a ceiling beyond which base change is required

mappings.target: Adapters / prompts over frozen base weights
residual_mismatches: ADAR is environment-driven automatically; adapters are chosen by an operator

outputs.public_translation: Octopuses keep their DNA fixed and retune their nerve proteins within hours by editing RNA when the water cools. The same shape shows up wherever a fast, reversible layer sits between fixed code and live output — adapters over a frozen AI model, acclimatization over a genome. The cost is the same too: the base has to stay frozen where the fast layer attaches.
outputs.uncertainty_statement: P3 (AI) and P4 untested; physical-scale mapping is a residual.
open_questions: Where is the ceiling of runtime recoding before base change is required?
Do the most input-facing parts of an AI system benefit most from runtime adaptation?
